episode.title: Preserve caller-owned conversation history while producing an extended result
episode.before: At parent c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880, run_conversation initialized its working message sequence with `messages = conversation_history or []`. A non-empty caller-supplied list was therefore reused by identity. The method subsequently appended the new user message and generated assistant messages to that same list, so resuming a conversation modified the caller's historical-state container in place.
episode.after: At 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3, run_conversation initializes its working sequence with `list(conversation_history)` when history is present, otherwise a new empty list. It can append the current turn to and return the working sequence while leaving the caller-owned outer history list unchanged. A regression test supplies two historical messages, runs one new turn, asserts that the input list retains its original length, and asserts that the returned message sequence is longer.
episode.diff: The merge changes the conversation initialization in run_agent.py from directly aliasing a supplied history list to making a shallow list copy. It also adds TestConversationHistoryNotMutated.test_caller_list_unchanged_after_run in tests/test_run_agent.py, using a mocked completion and patched persistence/resource side effects to verify that the input history length is unchanged while the returned history includes additional messages. The first-parent diff is 35 insertions and 2 deletions across run_agent.py and tests/test_run_agent.py.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3 is a merge titled `fix(agent): copy conversation_history to avoid mutating caller's list`; its message says it fixes issue #228, and its first parent is c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, and provenance.commit

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, run_conversation assigned `messages = conversation_history or []`, causing a non-empty supplied list to become the mutable working message list.
After the change, run_conversation assigns `messages = list(conversation_history) if conversation_history else []`, creating a distinct outer list for its working state.

run_conversation appends the current user message and final assistant message to `messages`, persists that sequence, and returns it in result[`messages`]; these operations explain why aliasing the caller's list caused mutation and why copying the list isolates the additions.
evidence_units.source: git show 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3:run_agent.py, user-message append following line 2820; final-message append at lines 3714-3717; persistence and result construction at lines 3786-3800

evidence_units.claim: Relative to the first parent, the implementation replaces direct history-list reuse with a shallow copy and adds a 33-line regression-test section; the merge stat reports 35 insertions and 2 deletions in two files.
evidence_units.source: git diff c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3 -- run_agent.py tests/test_run_agent.py; git show --stat 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3

evidence_units.claim: The added regression test passes a two-item history to run_conversation, records its original length, mocks a successful new answer, and asserts both that the caller's list length remains unchanged and that the returned message list has grown.

The regression test mocks the model response and patches session persistence, trajectory saving, and task-resource cleanup, isolating the list-ownership behavior from network and durable side effects.

The focused regression test could not be executed in the provided environment because the `pytest` executable is unavailable; validation is therefore based on direct inspection of the committed test rather than a fresh passing run.

candidate_atomics.name: isolate-caller-owned-sequence-before-extension
candidate_atomics.title: Copy caller-owned history before extending it
candidate_atomics.description: Create a distinct working sequence at the continuation boundary so additions for the new turn do not alter the caller's historical-state container.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a resumed operation to extend prior state and return the extended state without changing the caller-owned input sequence.
semantic_action.pre_state: A caller may supply a non-empty mutable sequence of prior messages, and the continuation routine will append new-turn messages to its working sequence.
semantic_action.post_state: The continuation routine's outer working sequence is distinct from the supplied sequence; new-turn appends appear in the returned sequence but not in the caller's input list.
semantic_action.validation: Provide a non-empty history, execute a completed new turn, then verify that the input sequence retains its original length while the returned sequence contains additional messages.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-input-preservation-and-output-extension
candidate_atomics.title: Verify preserved input and extended output
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise the continuation boundary with controlled side effects and check both halves of the ownership contract: unchanged caller state and an independently extended result.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent regression to input-list aliasing while confirming that conversation continuation still records the new turn.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continuation API accepts an existing mutable history and returns a message history after processing another turn.
semantic_action.post_state: The regression oracle demonstrates that the supplied history's outer length is unchanged and the returned history is longer than the original.
semantic_action.validation: Use a deterministic mocked completion, suppress persistence and cleanup side effects, call the continuation API, assert input length equality with the saved baseline, and assert returned length exceeds that baseline.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-caller-state-during-resume
candidate_workflows.title: Resume from history without corrupting caller-owned state
candidate_workflows.description: Establish an ownership boundary for a mutable history passed into a continuation routine, extend only a copied working sequence, and validate both preservation of the input and growth of the returned state.

workflow_graph.goal: Continue an operation from existing history while returning the newly extended history and preserving the caller's original history container.
when_to_use: A continuation or resume API accepts a caller-supplied mutable sequence and appends new state during processing.
Inspection or regression behavior shows that the routine aliases and mutates the caller's non-empty sequence.
anti_goals: Do not remove prior history from the working continuation state.
Do not suppress recording of the new user or assistant messages in the returned state.
Do not deep-copy or transform individual history entries unless nested-entry mutation is separately demonstrated and specified.
not_applicable_when: The API explicitly documents in-place mutation as part of its contract.
The supplied history is immutable or the routine never mutates the sequence structure.
The defect concerns mutation of nested message objects rather than append operations on the outer sequence.
inputs: continuation entry point that accepts prior history
deterministic completion or equivalent response fixture
workflow_graph.entry_state: A non-empty caller-owned history can be bound directly to the routine's working sequence, and later append operations can therefore corrupt the caller's preserved state.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The routine operates on a distinct outer sequence, preserves all supplied history entries for continuation, appends the new turn to the working result, and leaves the caller's input sequence structurally unchanged.

steps.condition: Apply when the continuation routine performs structural mutations such as append on a caller-supplied mutable sequence.
steps.validation: Inspect the initialization boundary and confirm that supplied history is copied into a distinct working sequence before any new-turn append occurs.

steps.condition: Run after the ownership boundary is changed and a deterministic completed-turn fixture is available.
steps.validation: Confirm that the caller's sequence length equals its pre-call baseline and that the returned sequence length exceeds that baseline.

validation_ladder: Static boundary check: the working outer sequence is constructed separately from a supplied mutable history.
Behavioral preservation check: after a completed new turn, the caller's history retains its original length.
Behavioral continuity check: the returned history is longer than the original, proving that isolation did not discard the new turn.
Focused automated regression test when the test runner and dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the API contract intentionally transfers ownership and permits in-place mutation.
Stop and broaden the investigation if individual pre-existing message objects are mutated, because a shallow sequence copy does not isolate nested objects.
Defer runtime confirmation if the repository's test runner or required dependencies are unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed test checks outer-list length, not object identity, exact preserved contents, or mutation of nested message dictionaries.
A fresh test execution is deferred because pytest is not installed in the supplied environment.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle lacks issue body, comments, PR body, reviews, and status checks, so motivation and acceptance details beyond the commit, implementation, and test cannot be independently recovered.
The implementation deliberately performs a shallow list copy; evidence does not establish whether nested message objects must also be isolated.
